Experimental. A group in Active Directory, and who is in it, run on a domain controller. Settings left unset are left as they are.

**Experimental.** Windows support is new, and this module may change between releases.

Use `windows_ad_group` to keep a group in Active Directory, and to make sure the right accounts are in it. Run it on a domain controller.

## Example usage

```hcl
step "app_admins" {
  windows_ad_group {
    name        = "AppAdmins"
    path        = "OU=Lab,DC=lab,DC=example,DC=com"
    scope       = "global"
    description = "Can manage the app"
    members     = ["alice", "ops"]
  }
}
```

With `authoritative`, the list is the whole group:

```hcl
step "web_servers" {
  windows_ad_group {
    name          = "WebServers"
    members       = ["web1$", "web2$"]
    authoritative = true
  }
}
```

## Arguments

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `authoritative` | bool | No | true makes members the complete list: anyone else is taken out. Never the login Conn3x uses, in a group it gets its rights through. |
| `category` | string | No | "security" or "distribution". Unset, a new group is a security group. |
| `description` | string | No | Description. |
| `members` | set of string | No | Accounts that must be in it, by sAMAccountName in this domain: users, groups, and computers with their trailing $, such as alice, ops or web1$. Others are left in unless authoritative is set. |
| `name` | string | Yes | Group name, used as both its name and its sAMAccountName, such as AppAdmins. |
| `on_remove` | string | No | What happens in the domain when this resource is removed: "forget" (default) leaves the group, "delete" deletes it. |
| `path` | string | No | Distinguished name of the OU or container it's in, such as OU=Lab,DC=lab,DC=example,DC=com. Unset leaves it where it is, and a new one goes to Windows' default, CN=Users. A group found elsewhere is moved. |
| `scope` | string | No | "domainlocal", "global" or "universal". Unset, a new group is global. |

## Read-only attributes

Conn3x sets these; reference them as `conn3x_windows_ad_group.<circuit>__<step>["<host>"].<name>`.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `in_sync` | bool | Whether the group matched at the last refresh. |
| `revision` | string | Changes each time Conn3x changes this on the host. Handlers watch it. |

A step lowers to the `conn3x_windows_ad_group` resource, one instance per host, and connects with its circuit's `ssh` block.

## How it works

**Names.** `name` is the group's name and its sAMAccountName, the name you'd type after `LAB\`. The group is found by that name anywhere in the domain, so if it's sitting in another OU and `path` is set, apply moves it.

**Waiting for AD.** Straight after a DC reboots, Active Directory can answer for the domain a minute before its global catalog does, and a write made in that minute can hang. So apply first waits until a query through the global catalog works too, for up to 10 minutes, then fails with the reason AD last gave. A write that gets no answer at all runs once more when AD answers again. It reads first, so it only writes what's still missing. A host that isn't a DC isn't waited on.

**Members.** Each member is a sAMAccountName in the same domain: `alice` for a user, `ops` for a group, `web1$` for a computer. Not `LAB\alice` and not a distinguished name, so there's only one way to write each account. Conn3x compares them by distinguished name, which means moving a user to another OU doesn't make the group drift.

By default, `members` are added and nobody else is taken out. With `authoritative = true` the list is complete, and anyone else is removed on apply. Accounts from other domains can't be listed yet; with `authoritative`, they'd be removed.

A member that doesn't exist yet, such as a user a later step makes, shows the group out of sync rather than failing the plan. At apply, a name that still doesn't resolve is an error. So put the users first, or chain the steps.

**Lockout guard.** Conn3x won't take its own login out of a group it gets its rights through, such as Domain Admins, so apply fails until the list keeps it.

**Scope and category.** Leave them unset and a new group is a global security group, as Windows makes one. A scope change between `global` and `domainlocal` goes through `universal`, because AD allows no direct step. AD refuses some changes anyway, such as making a group global while it has members from another domain.

**Drift.** A refresh reads the scope, category, description, location and members. A member added or removed by hand in Active Directory Users and Computers, or with `Add-ADGroupMember`, puts the step out of sync, and `conn3x drift` exits 2. Without `authoritative`, an extra member isn't drift.

## Removal

By default, deleting a `windows_ad_group` step leaves the group and its members. With `on_remove = "delete"` it deletes the group, unless the login Conn3x uses gets its rights through it.
